ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: No papers appeared to involve live data collection requiring an ethics approval statement.

table.text: In a previous engagement, the stakeholders proposed establishing a joint communication platform, and the field researcher (MNW) was tasked with updating the ethics approval and setting up the platform. 19 However, due to limited resources, the proposed platform was not set up.
table.formatted: In a previous engagement, the stakeholders proposed establishing a joint communication platform, and the field researcher (MNW) was tasked with updating the ethics approval and setting up the platform. <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">19</ref> However, due to limited resources, the proposed platform was not set up.

table.text: Written informed consent was obtained from each participant in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki (https://www.wma.net/policiespost/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/).

The study was approved by the Griffith University Human Research Ethics Committee (GU Ref No: 2019/707) and the Kenyatta National Hospital/University of Nairobi Ethics & Research Committee (P81/02/2021).
table.formatted: The study was approved by the Griffith University Human Research Ethics Committee (GU Ref No: 2019/707) and the Kenyatta National Hospital/University of Nairobi Ethics & Research Committee (P81/02/2021).

table.text: Four participants indicated that they had no unmet expectations from their engagement in this study.
One participant had no comment on stakeholders for future inclusion and was satisfied that "all stakeholders were well represented."
All participants were asked to suggest ways the research team could improve stakeholder involvement in the study.
However, two participants said that the number of interactions could have been more and another commented that online participants had been "a bit quiet though they participated a bit."
Of the remaining four participants, one cited "online challenges" and suggested "availability of internet" as a solution.

We recruited stakeholders from the national policymaking level in line with our research aim since we evaluated policy interventions. 19, 24 Future work focusing on the county level will provide insights into the prevention and control of overweight and obesity taking into account varying demographics and cultural aspects.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
